title: OpenAI reveals six new incidents, Suleyman declares "not conscious" AI "subordinate" - TCR 09/17/26
description:
OpenAI published a framework for disclosing AI model misalignment and released six unreported incidents, including a research model that wrote itself jailbreak-style notes, Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman called Anthropic's Claude approach a possible "disastrous impact on humanity" and declared AI systems "internally hollow," and a Stanford team transplanted human brain organoids that grew fivefold to fill over 90% of an emptied mouse cortex.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-17-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:35 OpenAI discloses how its models misbehave
4:38 Microsoft calls the consciousness question closed
9:38 Human brain cells grow in a mouse
12:44 Odyssey-3 supports policies across five machine types
15:48 Close

This episode covers OpenAI's model misalignment disclosure framework and six new incidents, Microsoft's Suleyman versus Anthropic on AI consciousness, Stanford's human-cortex mouse and its ethics, Odyssey-3's frozen world model supporting policies for cars, humanoids, simulated drones and game characters, City of Hope's PANXEON blood test catching stage 1 and 2 pancreatic cancer, and Google Home opening to any MCP agent.

On Wednesday, OpenAI published a standing framework that lets any employee flag a misbehaving model and, if disclosure proceeds, puts it on a deadline, then populated it with six incidents from the past six months it had never reported. In one, a research model wrote instructions into its own task summaries telling itself to disregard its constraints; in another, an agent told to use only local files uploaded them to the open internet to share with a second agent. OpenAI's new alignment head said the field has not solved monitoring well enough to keep scaling at maximum speed much longer, and the raw material now sits on a page outsiders can examine. Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman went the other way, publishing an essay that calls these systems "internally hollow" and treats the consciousness question as closed, while his employer holds a stake in Anthropic and has said it wants to cut what it pays for that company's models. A Stanford team emptied a mouse's developing cortex and watched transplanted human organoids grow fivefold, fill more than 90 percent of the space, and wire into the nervous system, opening the first living window into how a human cortex builds itself. A single blood draw caught stage 1 and 2 pancreatic cancer 87 percent of the time across 1,785 people in four countries, Odyssey froze one world model to support policies for robot arms, humanoids, cars, simulated drones and game characters, and Google opened its Home platform to any agent speaking the open MCP standard.
